dialogues.speaker: Gaudenty
dialogues.text: Everything's settled, right? What else do you want to know?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Your identity.

dialogues.speaker: Gaudenty
dialogues.text: Hey now, don't go asking questions you shouldn't. All you need to know is who I represent.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About those recon bots...

dialogues.speaker: Gaudenty
dialogues.text: Do you even know how much one of those can fetch on the black market? The offers that the merchants open with... You can't even imagine.

dialogues.speaker: Gaudenty
dialogues.text: Of course, on paper, my supervisors would never openly permit the sale of these recon bots. So quit obsessing over the payment — with the backdoor I can open for you, you'll make a fortune.

dialogues.speaker: Gaudenty
dialogues.text: By the by, you might not find recon bots at every location, because really, who knows if they'll stay where they are after going haywire...

dialogues.speaker: Gaudenty
dialogues.text: That said, you should find energy traces they've left behind. Cleaning those traces up is part of the order as well, so it must be done!

dialogues.speaker: Gaudenty
dialogues.text: Kuuvahki? Moonlanes? Who the heck even came up with these?

dialogues.speaker: Gaudenty
dialogues.text: If I actually understood that sort of tech, I wouldn't even need to...

dialogues.speaker: Gaudenty
dialogues.text: Ahem! When did you get here? If you have something to say, spit it out.

dialogues.speaker: Gaudenty
dialogues.text: Gathered quite a few parts this time, didn't you? Well then, I believe some recompense is in order. Could you help me dig up some intel?

dialogues.speaker: Gaudenty
dialogues.text: That Fontainian engineer's research is very interesting... She doesn't have to follow Aino around like a sick puppy. Has she ever considered going it alone?

dialogues.speaker: Gaudenty
dialogues.text: And don't ask me why I can't simply ask her myself. As an expatriate representative of the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau, I can't be seen asking engineers such invasive questions. Just imagine the size of that scandal...

dialogues.speaker: Gaudenty
dialogues.text: And could you please keep that fellow from the Adventurers' Guild away from me? As your client, I'm sure this request falls within the bounds of reason.

dialogues.speaker: Sarin
dialogues.text: #Hello, {NICKNAME}. Do you need my help with anything?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Tell me about Nod-Krai's Adventurers' Guild...

dialogues.speaker: Sarin
dialogues.text: The Guild here has a lot more trouble to deal with than anywhere else in Teyvat.

dialogues.speaker: Sarin
dialogues.text: But I chose to stay. And hey, from where I'm standing, I think Nod-Krai might be the best place for adventurers to be.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About this type of device...

dialogues.speaker: Sarin
dialogues.text: I'm ashamed to say this, but I admit I haven't formally studied this field. My design process was a patchwork of scattered techniques.

dialogues.speaker: Sarin
dialogues.text: I guess you could say it's a little... chimeric.

dialogues.speaker: Sarin
dialogues.text: Miss Aino's upgrades truly work wonders. Next time, I should test it out on tougher opponents.

dialogues.speaker: Sarin
dialogues.text: It's just marvelous... I designed a right piece of junk, but Miss Aino turned it into something truly formidable, just like that. Now, if we'd started with a machine designed by her instead...

dialogues.speaker: Sarin
dialogues.text: What would happen if her skills caught the eyes of some villains?

dialogues.speaker: Sarin
dialogues.text: After returning from the testing site, Ginette and I had a long chat.

dialogues.speaker: Sarin
dialogues.text: Meeting new friends, learning about new things... I guess that's par for the course for an adventurer.

dialogues.speaker: Sarin
dialogues.text: But the other guy off to the side... I wanted to talk to him, but once he saw me, he slipped away. How strange.

dialogues.speaker: Sarin
dialogues.text: Please keep an eye out for that expatriate representative for the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau. I swear I've seen him before... Something's off about him.

dialogues.speaker: Ginette
dialogues.text: Thank you so much for helping out with the troubleshooting!

response.speaker: Ginette
response.text: My robots were actually modified with devices that Aino invented, and the idea to use kuuvahki was based on one of her latest works. She's a total genius!

response.speaker: Ginette
response.text: I tried to do it myself, only to realize how difficult it actually was... I really have to learn from my seniors, don't I? Haha...

response.speaker: Ginette
response.text: Ah, those... Well, I'm not too proud to admit those initial malfunctions were all down to my "creativity." I wanted to try something novel, but ended up nearly ruining everything.

response.speaker: Ginette
response.text: But with the help of Aino's robots, even these "creative" experiments are still functioning smoothly. I have no clue how it all works, though...

dialogues.speaker: Letti
dialogues.text: Hello, how may I help?

response.speaker: Letti
response.text: You can just call me Letti. I'm also a member of Nod-Krai's Adventurers' Guild. After Gaudenty was arrested, the Branch Master asked me to meet with the workshop on his behalf.

response.speaker: Letti
response.text: After all, Miss Aino hasn't finished her research on the recon bots yet, and the Branch Master takes this very seriously.

choices.text: About things on the Fatui's end...

response.speaker: Letti
response.text: Don't worry. You can still use the Moonlanes you made, and there's no need for you to return the components you collected.

response.speaker: Letti
response.text: They seem to know that the person they found for the job wasn't reliable, so they don't intend to hold us accountable.
